title: Sustained pressure run notes — dec15 2026
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the notes from the ad-hoc sustained pressure run we kicked off 2026-12-15 (UTC) to reproduce a customer-observed throughput collapse at sustained QPS. Goal: replicate steady-state degradation, collect traces/metrics, and capture quick hypotheses for next steps.

Attendees:
- Aisha (owner) — ran orchestration and collection
- Diego — sampling/tracing, flamegraphs
- Hana — KV/cache telemetry and eviction traces
- Thomas — batching heuristics and scheduler
- Marta — release owner for recent kernel change (r1429)

Why we ran this:
- Multiple customers reported increasing p99 and sudden throughput drops after ~25–35 minutes into long jobs (samples come from Dedicated clusters N. Virginia).
- Local smoke runs (short 10m) didn't show it — appears to be a sustained-state issue.

Environment and quick config (what we executed):
- Cluster: dedicated-pressure-3 (nvme-backed, 8xA100-per-pod)
- Model: gptx-like-13b-q4a (variant used for reproducer)
- Runtime: serving-runtime @ r1429 (rolled 2026-12-12)
- Test harness: run_pressure v0.8.1 (internal)
- Command: run_pressure --duration 60m --qps 1800 --concurrency 400 --input-profile=customer-sampled-mix.json --seed=20261215 --kvcache=on --batching=dynamic
- Observability: p999,p99,p95,p50 token latency; GPU util; host memory; NIC drops; per-request KV hit/miss; sidecar GC events; scheduler queue depth.

What we saw (timeline):
- 0–5m: normal ramp — p50/p95 stable, GPU util ~62%, batching avg size 4.1 tokens/req.
- 5–20m: slight tail growth (p99 up ~12%) — attributed to transient queuing during burst windows.
- 25m: first throughput blip — drop of effective completed requests by ~28% for 60s, p99 spikes to 2.6x baseline.
- 26–35m: steady drift — throughput does not fully recover; average batching size decreases to ~2.3; KV cache hit-rate drops from 87% -> 61%; prefetch queue length climbs.
- 36–45m: periodic microbursts of latency correlated with host-level swap-in events on one pod (pod-3). We observed increased kernel pagefaults (~120/s spike) and an evicted KV shard.
- 45–60m: load rebalanced but overall throughput remained ~12–18% below baseline even after ramp-down.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV-cache pressure + eviction storm: evidence = sharp drop in per-request KV hit rate preceding throughput drop; eviction logs show concurrent TTL-driven evictions and a compactor run.
2) Scheduler-batching regression from r1429: change in scheduling window micro-optimizations may have reduced coalescing under sustained low-entropy streams; observed smaller average batch sizes later in the run.
3) Cross-pod memory pressure causing occasional OS page reclaim — correlated with pod-3 kernel pagefault spikes. Might be unrelated but amplifies tail.
4) Network NIC congestion during compactor/GC windows — small packet retransmits seen but not dominant.

Artifacts collected:
- Full perf traces for 6 pods (trace ids: trace-20261215-01..06) — uploaded to perf-bucket (s3://redwood-perf/pressure/2026-12-15/)
- KV eviction logs (kv-evict-20261215-p3.log)
- Flamegraphs: flame-p3-26m.svg, flame-p3-36m.svg
- Scheduler metrics snapshot: scheduler-sample-25m.json (time-series exported)
- Run harness log: pressure-run-20261215.log

Quick signal deep-dive (Diego/Hana findings):
- Diego: flamegraphs show long tail inside the GRPC read path during the drop window; stack traces point to repeated small RPCs to kv-shard service when cache miss storms occur. The cost of those RPCs is amplified because batching coalescing is lower.
- Hana: eviction pattern indicates async compactor kicks in when ephemeral allocations exceed threshold; compactor is O(n) and briefly spikes CPU and memory churn, and kicks other pods into page reclaim on nodes with tighter headroom.

Small experiments we ran in the same window:
- Disabled async compactor on a canary pod (pod-4) — pod-4 maintained higher KV hit-rate and did not show the throughput cliff; suggests compactor is a strong amplifier (not necessarily root cause).
- Forced larger scheduling window (--sched-window-ms=15 -> 25) for pod-2 — batching size recovered and p99 improved by ~18% under the same QPS.
- Replayed same workload on r1412 (previous runtime) on a small cluster: no collapse after 60m.

Preliminary conclusion:
- It's a multi-factor problem: the compactor / KV eviction storm seems to trigger additional RPCs which, combined with the scheduling micro-change in r1429 (smaller effective coalescing under certain request entropies), leads to reduced batching and a throughput collapse. OS-level page reclaim on certain hosts exacerbates tail but is not the initial trigger.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Aisha: assemble reproducer artifact + instructions and post to ENGINF-3245 (by 2026-12-16) — done (linked_artifacts).
- Marta: revert the scheduling micro-optimization in r1429 in a canary build and run a 2h sustained test (by 2026-12-18).
- Hana: add additional KV compactor telemetry (compactor start/finish, processed-keys, concurrent-run-count) and increase compactor backoff jitter (by 2026-12-20).
- Diego: instrument RPC paths for small KV misses to capture latency distribution at 1ms granularity (by 2026-12-17).
- Thomas: explore adaptive scheduler policy that increases coalescing window when observed KV miss-rate rises; prototype simulation by 2026-12-22.
- SRE (cc @oliver-roberts): evaluate node-level memory headroom and recommend kernel vm swappiness/tune adjustments for affected pools (by 2026-12-19).

Open questions we should answer next:
- Is the compactor itself doing any blocking I/O to remote storage during runs? Need IO traces.
- Could we short-circuit compactor triggers during high qps windows as a mitigation?
- Where does the cross-talk time boundary lie between compactor start and first visible throughput degradation? (we saw ~30s lead)

Suggested mitigations to try immediately in prod-safe ways:
- Canary revert of r1429 on a small dedicated pool (Marta) and observe for 48h.
- Temporarily bump scheduler window on Dedicated pools with the affected workload type (low-risk knob, reversible).
- Add KV compactor rate-limiter and jitter to prevent simultaneous kicks across shards.

Notes / misc (raw):
- Observed sample customer request shape attached (customer-sampled-mix.json) — low prompt entropy series with long prefix reuse, so KV should help a lot; when hits drop the impact is disproportionate.
- There are stray logs showing post-eviction client-side retries to the model host; investigating whether retry jitter is syncing.
- We should check GPU host memory cgroup limits on nodes where pagefaults observed.

Next meet: 2026-12-17 10:30 PT (perf sync) — plan is to review Marta's canary and Hana's compactor telemetry; Diego to present RPC micro-latency histograms.

Appendix: quick run commands used (for reproducibility)
- run_pressure --cluster dedicated-pressure-3 --duration 60m --qps 1800 --concurrency 400 --input customer-sampled-mix.json --kvcache=on --batching=dynamic --outdir /tmp/pressure-20261215
- collect_traces --trace-ids trace-20261215-* --dest s3://redwood-perf/pressure/2026-12-15/

If anything else is needed to be dumped into this file (more raw logs, kube yamls, perf counters), ping in slack #perf-team and I'll append.

— Aisha
